[b]The Pirn Parliament descended into chaos with MPs fighting each other.
[sub]Le Parlement de Pirn a sombré dans le chaos, les députés s'affrontant entre eux.[/b][/sub]
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────[/list]

[i][b]P I R N ─[/b][/i] On March 21, an extraordinary incident unfolded inside the [b]Pirn Parliament[/b] as lawmakers descended into a physical altercation after a sudden loss of composure. According to an account from a neutral member of parliament, tensions began when a legislator from the [b]Pirn People of Action Party (PPAP)[/b] was delivering a speech before the chamber. Several lawmakers from the opposition [b]Pirn Labor Party (PLP)[/b] abruptly stood up and began loudly booing the address.

At first, [b]Parliamentary Speaker[/b] [i]Margaret Horton[/i] managed to maintain order, calling on the dissenting MPs to show respect and remain quiet. However, the situation quickly escalated as more PLP members rose to join the heckling. The PPAP legislator at the podium eventually snapped, hurling insults at the PLP group, prompting fellow PPAP lawmakers to follow suit. The chambers order rapidly deteriorated.

The confrontation reached its peak when one PLP member suddenly removed a sandal and hurled it toward the PPAP benches. This act [i]broke the last dam,[/i] witnesses said, as PPAP members surged toward the PLP seats and both sides engaged in a full-blown brawl. Neutral lawmakers and members of the [b]Future Vision Party (FVP)[/b] reportedly panicked and attempted to flee, only to be pulled into the melee by PPAP and PLP members who mistook them for opponents. Speaker [i]Horton[/i] herself was dragged into the scuffle. Security forces eventually stormed the chamber to regain control, as the entire nation watched the chaos unfold live on television.

The incident exploded across social media. Young viewers mocked the spectacle, calling it a darkly comic reflection of Pirns politics, while analysts were sharply critical, accusing the PLP of disrespectful conduct and condemning the PPAP for failing to remain calm long enough for the Speaker to intervene. Both the PLP and PPAP later issued public apologies, but the brawl has left a deep blemish on Pirns political image domestically and abroad, with commentators describing it as [i]the worst parliamentary disaster they have ever witnessed.[/i] Many are now urging the parliament to strengthen internal security protocols after viewers noted the strikingly small number of guards present during the incident.

[b]March 15, 2028: On the Femboy Threat, A presentation to the Nation[/b]
Cahit Alparslan hated the sound of cameras, the flashing and the clicking; it disturbed his ears and annoyed his temperament. However, he had been called to make a special statement next to his counterpart, the Speaker of the Senate, on the new referendum, which was to take place in a month, regarding the threat of Alaqar and the Femboy faction that had taken power.
Clutching the papers that held his brief statement in his sweaty and meaty hands, he rolled himself to the podium, tapped the mic, and then spoke, his jowls jiggling, his lips smacking.
Today, he burbled, Today, I would like to announce that the enemies of Yzakastan have been shown with great vigor, he paused to take a breath, With great vigor they have been shown, that our democracy works also, he paused again, wheezing.

It is in this manner, that I am happy to announce that the Senate, he wheezed, And the house, his jowls jiggled, Have passed with great resolve, a bead of sweat rolled down his head as he dabbed it with a handkerchief, it was unusually humid that day, we have passed with great resolve, the war powers resolution! he clapped his hands together.
Polite applause filled the briefing room, with a few journalists shouting Glory to Yzakastan! 
Cahit Alparslan smiled, his jowls rippling like a flag, Glory to Yzakastan, Glory to the Shah, and glory to the people, he declared, wheezing and thumping the podium with his fat right hand.

[b]A meeting in the garden[/b]
Edis and Cahit found themselves once again in the garden courtyard of the shah, seated in wicker chairs around a table filled with tea and pastries. The shah sat across from the two men with a stern look on his face as he opened a red folder onto the table.
Gentlemen, the Council on Wartime Affairs has just finished briefing me on the viability of a war against Alaqar, and they urge caution against attacking Alaqar directly, he said.
Cahit snorted, Your honour, I find the Council of Wartime Affairs to be a liberalist hodgepodge of nonsense, founded upon the principles that this administration has explicitly sought to reject, he waved his hand for emphasis.
I would agree with the CWA, your honour, intoned Edis, A direct war would be disastrous to our forces, 
The shah nodded, I am inclined to agree with you, Edis, but let us look at the facts, he said, The armed forces of Alaqar consist of a total of 1.4 million soldiers, including reserves and auxiliary troops.
The Yzakastanian forces have what? 1.5 Million counting reserves? intoned Edis.
Yes, but while we have the numerical troop advantage by 100,000 or so, the equipment numbers are wildly separated, the government of Alaqar is more situated for a land-based defense, and wed be absolutely wipednot to mention they have two aircraft carrierswe have one, replied the shah.
Cahit frowned deeper, Why have we allowed this, this, our great nation, to fall into such a state? 
Nuclearisation, said Edis, But due to MAD, nuclearisation is not a tactic that we can afford to use anymore as a measure of balance, he continued.
A good point, replied the shah, So what do we do?
I propose an embargo, using the war powers, we can begin economic pressure on them, said Edis.
We dont have the international backing to enforce something like that, replied the Shah, eyeing Cahit, who had put his hands to his face and had begun to silently weep. 
How long would it take to acquire the necessary equipment? asked the Shah, looking at Edis.
Military? Oy vey, five, maybe six years, he replied.
At this point, Cahit had begun to weep aloud, tears running down his face, Edis moved to rub the statesman's back to console him.
The shah remained steel-faced and continued, War then, or at least direct conflict, is not an option, nor is it an option I believe the people will choose. Frankly, I am disappointed in our party for allowing this farce to continue. 
It was to appease the mullahs, replied Edis. 
D-mn the mullahs, stated the Shah, as Cahit continued to weep.
It was at the statement of curse against the mullahs that Cahit pounded the table, looking up, his eyes puffy, his cheeks jiggling, and in a strained voice, he declared, You insult the very system that helps aide our nation of stability, it is treason, TREASON, TREASON! he began to shake violently, his motorised chair shaking and jerking back as he trembled.
Calm Cahit, Calm, replied the shah.
YOU INSULT THE DIGNITY OF THIS NATION! he bellowed, YOU ARE A PUPPET OF THE CORPORATIONS, YOU SHALL BE TURNED INTO JAM, JAM, JAM DAMMIT! he roared, half up from his chair, wheezing, as Edis shouted at him to sit down.
Gentlemen, it was kind of you to come. It seems that our meeting is ended, stated the Shah calmly.
